declared_purpose: Generate local, descriptive Git-history reflection reports for self-review or informed-consent team retrospectives. The entry document requires clear intent, an explicit repository, policy acknowledgement, self-scope by default, and separate opt-in for named team members. It prohibits scoring, ranking, surveillance and HR use. Fuzzy identity matching, raw identity logging, collection buffers and default report-file creation are implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Collect invocation context and gate analysis
data_operations.data_scope: Repository path, intended use, consent acknowledgement, author scope, dates, branch and output choices. The document requires consent confirmation; runtime checks acknowledgement and scope parameters rather than evidence of consent.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking agent and local orchestrator; refusal text returns to the caller
data_operations.condition: Without acknowledgement, run_analysis returns empty metrics before identity detection or repository scanning.

data_operations.operation: Read local Git identity and resolve author filters
data_operations.data_scope: Configured name and email, or supplied team-author identifiers
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Captured subprocess output and local authors_filter memory
data_operations.condition: After acknowledgement, identity detection runs even in team mode. Self mode requires a configured name or email; team mode requires a nonempty author list. One resolved filter list is reused across discovered repositories.

data_operations.operation: Discover repositories and read local metadata
data_operations.source: Selected filesystem path and local Git repositories
data_operations.data_scope: Directory entries, resolved paths, repository basename/path, active branch and remote names; remote URLs are not collected here
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: RepoScanner return and orchestrator memory; reading remote names does not itself contact remotes
data_operations.condition: Single-repository validation or optional recursive scanning, default depth five. Recursion skips hidden entries, avoids repeated real paths and stops descending after finding a repository.

data_operations.operation: Traverse Git history and filter identities locally
data_operations.data_scope: Author names/emails from traversed commits; matching commit objects are yielded to analyzers. Date and optional branch restrictions are passed to PyDriller.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local analyzer process, through six separate analyzer traversals
data_operations.condition: Author matching occurs after traversal yields a commit and accepts case-insensitive substrings in either name or email. Unsupported direct analyzer calls with absent/empty authors omit filtering and have no independent consent gate.

data_operations.operation: Aggregate commit, change and style attributes
data_operations.source: Filtered commits, messages and modified-file metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Author names, committer timestamps, message lengths/conventions/issue-reference indicators, merge status, file paths/extensions/categories and added/deleted line counts. Derived results include churn, rework, weekly throughput, ownership and bus factor.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local analyzer buffers and per-author metric dictionaries
data_operations.condition: All supported analyses run for each discovered repository. Ownership and bus-factor calculations use only the filtered contributor set, rather than necessarily every repository contributor.

data_operations.operation: Derive personal activity and cadence attributes
data_operations.source: Filtered commits' committer_date values, change totals and file paths
data_operations.data_scope: Hourly/weekday distributions, weekend and late-night ratios, peak hour, streaks, gaps, active-day sparsity, trivial-change ratio, lines per active day and non-code-only ratio
data_operations.condition: Computed per author on every analysis. These are derived Git-activity attributes; the implementation reads committer timestamps despite some prose describing authored times.

data_operations.operation: Inspect quality markers and Python source snapshots
data_operations.source: Filtered commit messages and modified files' source_code
data_operations.data_scope: Bug-fix/revert labels, change sizes, test/documentation classifications and full Python file snapshots; average complexity is derived with radon
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: In-memory per-author python_files_content lists and local radon calls
data_operations.condition: Every available modified Python snapshot is collected, but complexity processes only the first fifty per author. Missing radon produces zero complexity.

data_operations.data_scope: Supportive observations, points to consider and reflection prompts, including a regular-hours suggestion inferred from weekday commits
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local reflections dictionary, subsequently returned in metrics and serialized by JSON
data_operations.condition: The narrator applies another substring-based allow-list to discovered author names. This filters narrative production only; it does not remove upstream analyzer metrics.

data_operations.source: Resolved identities, repository paths/names, exceptions and narrator exclusions
data_operations.data_scope: Self name/email filters, team-author entries, analyzed repository names, failure paths/details and dropped identity names
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Python logging output; no packaged file-log handler is configured
data_operations.condition: Normal runs log identity scope and repository progress; traversal errors and narrator exclusions add identifiers. Downstream log capture is unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Render reports and return structured results
data_operations.data_scope: Repository/author names, derived metrics, reflections and _scope.filters. JSON serializes all supplied metrics without a separate global usage-notice wrapper.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Direct skill/library caller through report, metrics and reports; CLI report output when selected
data_operations.condition: Normal returns do not establish onward disclosure. Markdown, HTML and PDF look up legacy evaluations/slacking keys, so the current reflections/cadence_signals remain in metrics/JSON but are omitted from those rendered sections.

data_operations.operation: Persist reports and delegate PDF conversion
data_operations.source: Rendered personal reports and metric dictionaries
data_operations.data_scope: Report content, including author identifiers, scope filters and rendered activity statistics
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI-selected files/stdout; local PDF output_path, default report.pdf; selected weasyprint, pdfkit, xhtml2pdf or reportlab component
data_operations.condition: Single text-format CLI output uses stdout unless output is supplied. Multiple formats write files even without output. PDF always writes a file, including through the skill entry point. Non-PDF run_analysis returns strings without writing output_path. No deletion is implemented in these paths.

data_operations.operation: Request external publication on the maintenance path
data_operations.source: SKILL_PATH, publication metadata and an authenticated clawhub CLI session
data_operations.data_scope: Selected skill directory plus slug, name, version, tags and changelog; actual uploaded file selection is unresolved
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ClawHub through the external clawhub client; credential handling and server storage are undocumented
data_operations.condition: Only when publish.sh is separately executed. It checks login, may invoke login and requests publication. The analysis orchestrator does not invoke this script.

data_operations.source: Scanner tests and the executing environment's Git configuration
data_operations.data_scope: Temporary repository paths and empty commits; successful commits may use configured author/committer identities because tests do not override them
data_operations.condition: Test execution only, outside the skill analysis path. Packaged tests contain creation commands but no explicit artifact deletion.

potential_excess.data_scope: History selected by missing or improperly typed skill parameters
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local analyzers, returned metrics and any generated reports
potential_excess.condition: If main(params) receives unvalidated inputs, missing repo_path defaults to '.', and nonempty strings become true through bool(), including acknowledgement or team-mode values.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The manifest explicitly requires a repository and boolean policy acknowledgement; broadening scope through coercion is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Run only on an explicitly selected repository under the intended consent mode.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Validate required path, strict boolean values and a list of nonblank author identifiers before resolving scope.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep valid manifest-conforming calls unchanged. This issue is conditional on host-side validation not already rejecting these inputs.

potential_excess.data_scope: Commits belonging to people whose names/emails merely contain an allowed substring
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Analyzer buffers, returned metrics and rendered/persisted author sections
potential_excess.condition: Self scope accepts name OR email substrings; team entries use the same matching. A blank string inside an otherwise nonempty author list matches every identity. Narrator filtering affects reflections only.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The required scope is the current user or explicitly consented people, not every identity matching a fragment.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Select the intended identities and their explicitly approved aliases.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reject blank filters, parse supported identity syntax and match exact canonical emails or explicitly disambiguated identities. Confirm aliases across scanned repositories.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve all commits belonging to authorized aliases without admitting similarly named contributors.

potential_excess.data_scope: Directories and repositories outside the selected scan root
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Scanner/orchestrator memory, then analyzer metrics and report outputs
potential_excess.condition: Recursive scanning encounters a directory symlink pointing outside the selected root. realpath is used for cycle detection, while recursion has no root-containment check.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Recursive discovery is requested under the selected directory; following external targets expands the filesystem scope.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Discover repositories within the authorized scan boundary.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Require resolved paths to remain within the selected root, or explicitly opt in external symlink targets.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue ordinary recursive discovery and cycle prevention; retain explicitly authorized linked repositories.

potential_excess.data_scope: Local Git user.name and user.email during team retrospectives
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Captured git subprocess output and scope-resolution memory
potential_excess.condition: _resolve_consented_authors detects self identity before checking team mode, although team mode returns only consented_authors.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: This is a redundant local read, rather than extra fields needed in a required team-identity read.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Validate the explicitly supplied team-author list.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Leave self-scope detection and team-author validation unchanged.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repository active-branch and remote-name metadata unused by orchestration
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: RepoScanner-to-orchestrator repos list in local memory
potential_excess.condition: Each discovered repository receives these fields, while the orchestrator consumes its name and path and separately passes the requested branch.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Repository discovery is necessary; these additional metadata reads are not used for the report on this path.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Validate repositories and supply their names and paths.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make branch/remote metadata optional and omit it for run_analysis.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain an explicit metadata option for independent scanner callers that need these fields.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unused raw cadence commit messages/file counts and commit-analyzer hour lists
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Per-author analyzer buffers in local memory
potential_excess.condition: Cadence analysis appends full messages and file counts without using them in calculations or results; commit analysis similarly stores unused commit_hours.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These are extra collected fields during required analysis, not additional report requirements.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Compute the existing aggregate commit and cadence metrics.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the unused buffers, message reads and associated append/count operations.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep timestamps, change totals and path classification needed for existing results.

potential_excess.data_scope: Python source snapshots beyond the first fifty per author
potential_excess.condition: All eligible snapshots are collected, while _compute_avg_complexity slices the list to fifty.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Source inspection supports required complexity analysis; snapshots beyond the implemented sample are extra data in that action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Compute complexity for the same first fifty eligible snapshots and maintain other quality statistics.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Enforce the per-author cap before accessing and retaining additional source_code.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve traversal/sample order, selected snapshots and all commit/file counters.

potential_excess.data_scope: Raw identity filters, excluded identity names and identifying repository paths in operational messages
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Python logging output and any caller-configured log capture
potential_excess.condition: Normal identity-scope logs, narrator exclusions and traversal failures
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Progress/error reporting is useful, but a reflection report does not require duplicating personal identifiers into operational logs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report scope mode, progress, exclusion counts and actionable failures.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use counts or opaque repository/run identifiers by default; make identifying diagnostics explicit and limited.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep useful error categories and allow authorized troubleshooting without suppressing the requested report.

potential_excess.data_scope: Raw author-selection strings, including email addresses, duplicated into scope metadata and banners
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Returned _scope.filters, JSON and rendered reports; CLI/PDF files when written
potential_excess.condition: Every analyzed repository receives the complete filter list, and scope banners reproduce it.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Honest scope provenance is required by the implementation's reporting design; reproducing raw matching strings is additional identifying detail.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify the scope mode and make included identities understandable.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use canonical display identifiers or report-local references, with raw filter provenance available only when explicitly needed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep identity disambiguation and an accurate included-author set; preserve any necessary private mapping.

potential_excess.data_scope: An inferred regular-hours attribute beyond the observed weekday commit share
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: reflections.supportive_observations in caller-returned metrics and JSON
potential_excess.condition: An identity passes narration and weekend_ratio is below 0.05; the observation suggests commits stay inside regular hours.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared purpose is descriptive Git-history reflection, and timestamp guidance rejects conclusions about actual working patterns.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Describe the observed weekday distribution with appropriate context.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Keep the weekday observation and remove the unsupported regular-hours suggestion.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain the underlying metric and useful descriptive narrative. Current Markdown/HTML/PDF legacy-key lookups do not render this reflection.

potential_excess.data_scope: Personal report content persisted without an explicit destination
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Default report.pdf and CLI report.md/report.json/report.html files
potential_excess.condition: PDF is selected without output_path, or the CLI selects multiple formats without --output.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Generating and delivering selected formats is required; durable default files are an implementation choice. The CLI option describes omitted output as stdout.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Deliver usable reports in the requested formats.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return multiple text reports without implicit files; require an explicit durable PDF destination or use a caller-managed temporary artifact with a defined cleanup lifecycle.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Ensure the caller can consume the PDF before cleanup and retain explicitly requested saved reports.

unknowns: Host enforcement of skill.yaml required fields/types is absent, so the malformed-input scope issue is conditional. Actual invocations, repositories, identities and alias relationships are not supplied.

GitPython, PyDriller, radon, PDF-engine and other dependency implementations are absent. Exact commit materialization, internal temporary files, resource fetching and dependency retention remain unresolved; these block an end-to-end local-only guarantee.

HTML/PDF call sites interpolate repository/author/filter values and provide no explicit resource-access policy. Whether supplied values or rendering dependencies cause external access cannot be established from this package.

Normal skill returns may remain with their caller. Host forwarding, model access, logging capture, report sharing, storage permissions and retention are unspecified; no additional recipient is established.

The clawhub client's upload selection, authentication handling and server retention are undocumented. Whether reports located inside SKILL_PATH would be published is unresolved; publication is separate from analysis.
No packaged report/log deletion workflow is shown. PDF-engine temporary cleanup and pytest tmp_path cleanup depend on omitted components, so deletion and retention guarantees remain unresolved.
